correctness.rationale: After reducing to center-passing lines by the cited theorem, every such line falls into exactly one of two side-incidence classes. If it meets the horizontal sides at symmetric offsets, one half contains a boundary pair at distance at least \(\sqrt{A^2+4B^2}\), with equality only at zero offset. If it meets the vertical sides, one half contains a pair at distance at least \(\sqrt{4A^2+B^2}\), which is no smaller because \(A\ge B\). The vertical midpoint cut produces a half-rectangle whose diameter is exactly \(\sqrt{A^2+4B^2}\). Equality conditions give the stated straight-line uniqueness. No numerical experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The rectangle is the canonical two-parameter centrally symmetric polygon and a natural first nonsymmetric-by-quarter-turn family in the maximum-relative-diameter fencing problem. The result gives a complete exact optimization for every aspect ratio and resolves the optimal center-line direction in this family, directly addressing the literature’s stated lack of a precise optimal-line characterization. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a recomputation of the square alone.
